# Didache Chapter 5 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Hierosolymitanus (H), Didache 5 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/DID_005_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 5

**1** But the way of death is this: first of all it is evil and full of curse — murders, adulteries, lusts, sexual immoralities, thefts, idolatries, magic arts, sorceries, robberies, false testimonies, hypocrisies, duplicities, craftiness, arrogance, malice, self-will, greediness, foul speech, jealousy, insolence, pride, boastfulness;

**2** persecutors of the good, haters of truth, lovers of lies, not knowing the reward of righteousness, not adhering to the good nor to righteous judgment, keeping awake not for the good but for the evil — from whom meekness and patience are far off; lovers of vain things, pursuing reward, having no mercy for the poor, not laboring for the oppressed, not knowing him who made them, murderers of children, destroyers of the image of God, turning away from one who is in need, oppressing the afflicted, advocates of the wealthy, unjust judges of the poor — altogether sinful. Children, may you be delivered from all of these.

---

*EMET notes: Chapter 5 is a single extended catalog of vices constituting the "way of death." The Greek is one sustained breathless list. "Murderers of children" (φονεῖς τέκνων) may refer to both abortion/infanticide and to those who abandon children. "Destroyers of the image of God" (φθορεῖς πλάσματος θεοῦ) — πλάσμα = that which is formed/molded; a direct allusion to Gen 2:7 (God forming humanity). The closing "Children" (τέκνα) is an address — matching the "My child" of ch. 3-4.*
